description: This horizontal bar chart from the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models” illustrates the number of tasks (# tasks) associated with different language families, with the bars arranged vertically along the y-axis in descending order of task count. The x-axis, labeled “# tasks,” represents the quantity of tasks and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each bar corresponds to a language family, with the longest bar at the top representing “IE-Slavic” with approximately 44 tasks, followed by “IE-Romance” at about 38 tasks, “IE-Germanic” at around 35 tasks, “Uralic” at roughly 11 tasks, “IE-Baltic” at approximately 10 tasks, “IE-other” at about 8 tasks, “IE-Indic” at roughly 7 tasks, “Semitic” at around 6 tasks, “Turkic” at approximately 4 tasks, and the shortest bar at the bottom, “Austronesian,” at about 2 tasks. The bars are colored differently for each language family: IE-Slavic is light blue, IE-Romance is dark blue, IE-Germanic is light green, Uralic is pink, IE-Baltic is red, IE-other is light orange, IE-Indic is dark orange, Semitic is lavender, Turkic is purple, and Austronesian is dark purple. The bars are not grouped or stacked but are presented individually, and there is no visual emphasis such as shading or bolding applied to any specific bar.
